hints: Look at what the right-hand arrow actually makes from the elements at the top, it forms more than just carbon dioxide.

Split that right-hand change into two separate formations, $\text{C(s) + O}_2\text{(g)} \rightarrow \text{CO}_2\text{(g)}$ and $2\text{H}_2\text{(g) + O}_2\text{(g)} \rightarrow 2\text{H}_2\text{O(l)}$.
Remember formation means 1 mole of compound from elements, so ask how many moles of water are formed and whether any sign needs flipping for this downward arrow.
walkthrough:
**Read the cycle with Hess's Law**

Think of the top box as the starting elements and the bottom right box as the finish. By Hess's Law, the enthalpy change is independent of route, so the right-hand arrow must take us all the way from elements to products.

Top to bottom-right: $$\text{C(s) + 2H}_2\text{(g) + 2O}_2\text{(g)} \rightarrow \text{CO}_2\text{(g) + 2H}_2\text{O(l)}$$

**Split the right-hand arrow into two formations**

This one arrow is really doing two formation reactions at the same time. One is carbon forming carbon dioxide, the other is hydrogen forming water.

$$\text{C(s) + O}_2\text{(g)} \rightarrow \text{CO}_2\text{(g)} \quad \Delta H = \Delta H_f^\ominus \text{CO}_2\text{(g)}$$ $$2\text{H}_2\text{(g) + O}_2\text{(g)} \rightarrow 2\text{H}_2\text{O(l)} \quad \Delta H = X$$

**Identify X as formation of water**

By definition, enthalpy of formation of water is for this reaction with 1 mole:
$$\text{H}_2\text{(g) + } \tfrac{1}{2}\text{O}_2\text{(g)} \rightarrow \text{H}_2\text{O(l)}$$ 
We need 2 moles of $\text{H}_2\text{O(l)}$, so we need twice this value. The arrow is in the formation direction (elements to compound), so no sign change is needed.

$$X = +2 \times \Delta H_f^\ominus \text{H}_2\text{O(l)}$$

options.A: Incorrect. Combustion of 1 mole of $\text{H}_2$ does make 1 mole of $\text{H}_2\text{O}$, so it is numerically equal to formation of water, but we only burn 2 moles of $\text{H}_2$, not 4. The 4 comes from mistakenly counting H atoms instead of $\text{H}_2$ molecules.
options.B: Incorrect. Like A, this uses 4 instead of 2, counting H atoms as $\text{H}_2$ molecules. It also flips the sign. Combustion of hydrogen is exothermic (negative), so +4 times would give a large positive value, opposite to the exothermic formation of water.
options.C: Incorrect. The magnitude 2 is right because 2 moles of $\text{H}_2\text{O(l)}$ are formed, but the minus sign is wrong. The right-hand arrow goes from elements down to compounds, which is the formation direction itself, so we add $+2 \times \Delta H_f$, not subtract it.
options.D: Correct. Well done. The right-hand route forms 1 mole of $\text{CO}_2$ plus 2 moles of $\text{H}_2\text{O}$. So total enthalpy is $\Delta H_f^\ominus \text{CO}_2 + 2 \times \Delta H_f^\ominus \text{H}_2\text{O}$. Therefore X is +2 times the enthalpy of formation of water.
